validity.researcher_notes: Comanche Trail Pipeline's San Elizario Crossing is part of the same certificated project as the Waha-to-San Elizario mainline: FERC authorized construction of a 42-inch-diameter pipeline, about 1,086 feet long, via horizontal directional drill under the Rio Grande near San Elizario, TX, transporting gas to 'a new delivery interconnection near the City of San Isidro, in the Mexican state of Chihuahua' where it ties into the Ojinaga-to-El Encino system (naturalgasintel.com, 'Comanche's San Elizario Border Crossing Gets FERC Thumbs-Up'). EIA's 'New U.S. border-crossing pipelines bring shale gas to more regions in Mexico' (todayinenergy, id=28972) independently names Comanche Trail among the pipelines built specifically to cross into Mexico via this corridor. The flagged endpoint (31.559, -106.277) is ~4.4 km from San Elizario, TX, consistent with the drawn line reaching a real interconnect point just across the river rather than a boundary-precision artifact. This is a sheet-classification question, not a geometry fix, so no coordinates are proposed. Only 'endpoint_country' was flagged for this row (not 'countries'), so this record addresses that one field per the worklist.
